text: Lessons 13 and 14 each built one Test. In any real application, that's never the whole picture — a single feature needs several Tests covering different scenarios. A Test Suite is ATF's answer: a real grouping of multiple individual Tests that run together as one coordinated set, with one combined pass-fail result.

The obvious benefit is not clicking Run Test five separate times, but the deeper value is coherence. A change rarely affects just one narrow scenario — a Business Rule change on one table can plausibly affect several related workflows at once. Running the related group together is what actually makes regression testing practical as an application grows.

A Test Suite still has to be run by something. Running it only when a human remembers leaves the exact gap Lesson 12 described wide open — nobody tests on the days nobody happens to think of it. Scheduled Test Execution closes that gap — a Suite runs automatically on a defined schedule, the same underlying idea Course 3 covered as Scheduled Jobs: a server-side task that fires on its own, with no user present to trigger it.
A Test Suite scheduled to run nightly runs every single night, whether or not anyone on the team is thinking about testing that day, or even logged into the instance at all.

This is the chapter's real payoff. Lesson 12 opened with silent regressions discovered late, from a support ticket, rather than caught early. A nightly scheduled Suite run catches a regression the very next night, as a failed Test result someone can investigate immediately.
Grouping and scheduling is what turns individual Tests into an actual safety net. Next up: the ATF Lab, building real test coverage for the Equipment Checkout capstone application from Course 6.
